A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the optimal design in each class is a 2n factorial design with a specific arrangement of the levels of the factors in the design, with n being the number of levels of each factor, and with the levels of each factor being replicated in each of the n other factors.
the optimal designs d1 for the four classes are all orthogonal designs, i.e. they are optimal with respect to all four criteria.
the optimal designs d1 are of the form of 2n factorial designs in which the n factors are split into two sets of m = n/2 factors, each set of which is assigned to one of the two treatments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for the optimal designs d1 in the first three classes, the number of treatments n in the design is the same as that in the design d1 in the last class.
for 2n-factorial paired comparison experiments with n≥4 factors, the optimal design is a typical design of class 1.

for the typical design in the i-th design class, the optimal design d1 is a 2n-factorial design with the same structure as the design in the i- th class, but with a different allocation of the n2 observations, i= 1,2,3,4.
